title: Asking Politely: Could, Would, and May
summary: Learn how to ask for things nicely in English. You will use could, would, and may in daily life.

sections.p: We use 'could' to ask for something in a polite way. It is softer and nicer than saying 'can'. You can use this when talking to people you do not know well, or in shops and restaurants. It is very common and helpful for daily life.

sections.h: Using Would for Offers and Wishes
sections.p: We use 'would' to ask polite questions about what someone wants. We often say 'Would you like...?' when we offer food, drinks, or help to a friend or a customer. It is a very polite and friendly way to speak.

ex.en: Would you like a cup of tea?

sections.p: We use 'may' when we want to ask for permission in a very polite or formal way. It is great for offices, hotels, or speaking to teachers and bosses. It sounds a little more serious than 'could', but people use it every day.

tip: Think of 'May' as wearing a nice suit for a special meeting, and 'Could' and 'Would' as your friendly everyday clothes!

quiz.en: ___ you help me carry this heavy bag, please?

quiz.ask: Choose the formal word for asking permission
Select the correct polite offer start

quiz.en: ___ you please tell me the time?
